title: Scripture: God removes, transfers, deletes, casts sins into the sea
source_text: II. Nam Scriptura Sacra, Dei erga homines bonitatem commendans, saepe testatur eum fidelium peccata tollere, transferre, delere, imo projicere in profundum maris. Ita Moses in Exodo hanc Deo gloriam tribuit: Domine Deus, misericors & clemens, patiens & multae miserationis, ac verax, qui custodis misericordiam in millia, qui aufers iniquitatem, & scelera atque peccata, Exod. 34. Quod imitatus Michaeas Propheta, Quis Deus, inquit, similis tui, qui aufers iniquitatem, & transfers peccatum reliquiarum haereditatis tuae? Non immittet ultra furorem suum, quoniam volens misericordiam est. Revertetur & miserebitur nostri, deponet iniquitates nostras, & projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra. Mich. 7. Quibus verbis alludit Propheta ad Aegyptios, populi Dei hostes, quos Deus olim aquis rubri maris obruit, & in profundum illius submersit.
pass_a_gloss: For Sacred Scripture, recommending God's goodness toward men, often testifies that he takes away, transfers, deletes, even casts the faithful's sins into the depth of the sea. Thus Moses in Exodus attributes this glory to God: Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true, who keeps mercy unto thousands, who takes away iniquity and crimes and sins (Exodus 34). Which Micah the Prophet imitated: Who is a God like you, who takes away iniquity and transfers the sin of the remnant of your inheritance? He will not send forth his fury again, for he wills mercy. He will return and pity us, put away our iniquities, and cast all our sins into the depth of the sea (Micah 7). By which words the Prophet alludes to the Egyptians, enemies of God's people, whom God once overwhelmed with the waters of the Red Sea and submerged in its depth.
pass_b_english: Scripture often says God takes away, transfers, deletes, even casts the faithful's sins into the sea (Exodus 34; Micah 7).
Micah's sea-image alludes to Egypt drowned in the Red Sea.
